anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the +12V rail (barrel-jack input) is tied to global net NET0005, which feeds fan-header pins 2/3 of J1 and J7. On the MCU sheet the same global net NET0005 is connected to ESP32-C3 pin 30 (GPIO20/U0RXD) together with a 10 k pull-up (R7) to +3V3 and a TVS diode (D5) to GND. Thus the 12 V supply rail and the 3.3 V GPIO/fan-tach input net are merged.
anomalies.expected: The fan-tach / GPIO20 input should sit on its own low-voltage net pulled up to +3V3 and clamped by a TVS, while the fan supply pins 2/3 should be on the +12V net; the two must not share a net. The spec describes the tach inputs as 'TVS-diode-protected inputs' on the 3.3 V logic side, never on 12 V.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (page 7): '+12V' arrow -> node -> 'NET0005' -> J1/J7 Conn_01x04 pins 2,3
MCU sheet (page 3): 'NET0005' on U5 pin 30 (GPIO20/U0RXD) with R7 10K to +3V3 and D5 D_TVS to GND
Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs

anomalies.impact: 12 V is applied directly to a 3.3 V GPIO (GPIO20/U0RXD) and to its 3.3 V pull-up and ground-clamp TVS, which will forward-conduct the TVS, fight the pull-up, and likely damage the MCU or the UART RX; the second fan tach is also shorted to 12 V and non-functional.

anomalies.observed: The WS2812B status LED D6 has its data input pin 2 (DIN) wired to net NET0004, but NET0004 appears nowhere else in the drawing; no ESP32 pin (or any other component) carries NET0004. The LED's VDD and GND are connected, but DIN is left floating.
anomalies.expected: The onboard WS2812B status LED's DIN must be driven from an ESP32 GPIO, as the spec states the board 'exposes status over ... a single onboard WS2812B status LED'.

evidence.quote: MCU sheet (page 3): 'D6 WS2812B' pin 2 'DIN' -> 'NET0004' (NET0004 has no other connection on any sheet)
a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1)

anomalies.impact: The status LED cannot be addressed by the firmware; the Wi-Fi status indication via the onboard LED is lost.

anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the AP63203WU buck U8 bootstrap pin 6 (BST) is tied through C4 (100 nF) to GND, and there is no capacitor between BST and the switching node pin 5 (SW). The reference design's bootstrap cap is therefore absent/misconnected.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, 'U8 SW(5) drives the buck inductor L1 (3.9 µH) and bootstrap cap C13' — the bootstrap capacitor must connect BST to SW, not to GND, to provide high-side gate drive.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (page 7): U8 pin 6 'BST' -> C4 100nF -> GND; pin 5 'SW' -> L2 3.9uH with no BST-SW cap
U8 SW(5) drives the buck inductor L1 (3.9 µH) and bootstrap cap C13

anomalies.impact: Without a proper BST-SW bootstrap capacitor the high-side MOSFET cannot be turned on, so the 3.3 V rail may fail to start or regulate, starving the MCU and peripherals.
